rule_title: Tests come with features — Rule 3a end-to-end fixture testing
message: Commit 23d548d (kitchensink r0023 test_forge) is a test-forge round and adds many strict numeric-threshold assertions, but every new e2e test still drives the pipeline through the in-process `_record_fixture(tmp_path)` helper which calls `fake_llm` / `fake_tool` synthetic stubs. There is no committed, real recorded-trace JSON fixture under tests/fixtures/ for this record/replay library — the canonical end-goal artifact for stepback. Rule 3a calls for at least one e2e test using a REAL fixture per round; for stepback that is a captured trace JSONL from an actual LLM/tool session (or at minimum a checked-in golden trace produced once and replayed). The new test_e2e_replay tests still synthesize the trace at test-time from fake_llm rather than loading a recorded artifact.
evidence: ls tests/fixtures/ → __init__.py, agent.py, parallel_agent.py (no .jsonl/.json/.sbb golden traces)
tests/test_e2e_replay.py new tests all start with `path, key = _record_fixture(tmp_path)` (synthesized in-test, not a committed fixture)
tests/fixtures/agent.py defines fake_llm/fake_tool stubs rather than a recorded session

rule_title: Rule 3b — TEST-FORGE round must catch real defects, not introduce flake
message: test_e2e_replay.py::test_replay_speedup_vs_record_is_measurable asserts `replay_time < record_time * 2.0 + 0.05`. Wall-clock comparisons on tiny in-process traces are notoriously flaky on shared CI runners — record_time and replay_time can both be sub-millisecond, and a 50ms slack is small relative to GC/scheduler jitter. Per Rule 3b, mutation-killing strictness is the goal, but a flaky timing assertion is an anti-test in disguise: it will eventually fail unrelated to any real regression and erode trust. Prefer asserting `result.real_executions == 0` (already present and sufficient) and drop the wall-clock inequality, OR widen the tolerance and mark the test with a stable repeat budget.
evidence: Same test already asserts result.real_executions == 0 and result.cache_hit_count == 12 — those are the deterministic invariants that prove the cache-hit path; the timing assertion adds flake without adding mutation-kill power.

rule_title: Rule 3 — vacuous-style assertions slipped into new strict tests
message: Two of the new strict-threshold tests still contain `assert found is not None` (test_e2e_replay.py:210, 357) immediately followed by stronger structural assertions. Per Rule 3b's anti-test guidance ('vacuous `assert x is not None` is an anti-test'), the not-None line is redundant — the subsequent `.step_id == "step:12"` access would itself raise on None. Removing or replacing with a typed assertion would reduce noise. Severity: advisory because the surrounding assertions are strong; the not-None lines are merely dead-weight, not actively wrong.

rule_title: Repo hygiene — committed __pycache__ churn (carry-over, not introduced this round)
message: The commit's name-status shows ~14 .pyc files under stepback/__pycache__/ and tests/__pycache__/ being modified (Bin churn for both cpython-311 and cpython-314 variants). The current commit did not ADD them — they were checked in by an earlier round (544be11) — but every round now produces meaningless byte-identical-or-near-identical Bin diffs that bloat reviewability. There is still no .gitignore. Recommend a one-line follow-up commit to `git rm -r --cached **/__pycache__ .DS_Store` plus add a standard Python .gitignore. Not fatal because no constitution rule is broken by this commit alone, but it actively undermines the auditability the constitutional/critic round depends on.
